section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Connecticut?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Connecticut requires applicants to be at least 16 years old to apply for a learner's permit — one of the older permit ages in the United States. Most states allow permits at 15 or 15½, making Connecticut's 16-year minimum a state-specific fact commonly tested on the CT DMV exam.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for adult drivers (age 21+) in Connecticut?
note: Connecticut's per se DUI limit is 0.08% BAC for adult drivers. Reaching 0.08% is itself sufficient for a DUI charge regardless of apparent impairment. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Connecticut's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a permit holder complete before upgrading to a restricted license?
options: a:20 hours,b:30 hours,c:40 hours,d:50 hours
note: Connecticut law requires a minimum of 40 hours of supervised, behind-the-wheel driving practice before a 16- or 17-year-old permit holder can apply for a driver's license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Connecticut requires a learner's permit holder to hold the permit for how long before applying for a restricted license?
options: a:3 months,b:6 months,c:9 months,d:12 months
note: Connecticut requires permit holders to hold the learner's permit for at least 6 months (180 days) before applying for a restricted operator's license at age 16½. This holding period ensures permit holders gain adequate supervised experience.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Connecticut law, what curfew restriction applies to licensed 16- and 17-year-old drivers?
options: a:They cannot drive between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM.,b:They cannot drive between 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM.,c:They cannot drive between Midnight and 5:00 AM.,d:They cannot drive after 9:00 PM.
note: In Connecticut, licensed drivers who are 16 or 17 years old are prohibited from driving between 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM, unless traveling for employment, school, religious activities, or medical necessity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on urban streets in Connecticut when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Connecticut's default speed limit in urban areas is 25 mph when no other limit is posted. In business and residential districts, the default is specifically set at 25 mph — drivers should not assume a higher speed is legal without a posted sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Connecticut highway and see an emergency vehicle pulled over with flashing lights. What does the Move Over law require?
options: a:Honk and slow to 20 mph,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safe; if not, slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely until the vehicle leaves,d:Only move over for police — not tow trucks or utility workers
note: Connecticut's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, fire, or towing vehicle with flashing lights. If a lane change is not safe, slow to a reasonable and safe speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Connecticut, when must you stop for a pedestrian?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk,b:Whenever a pedestrian is crossing or about to cross the roadway at a crosswalk — marked or unmarked,c:Only when a pedestrian signal is present,d:Only when the pedestrian is in your direct lane of travel
note: Connecticut law requires drivers to yield to and stop for pedestrians at all crosswalks — including unmarked intersections. Any intersection where two roads meet is legally a crosswalk even without painted lines. Failing to yield to a pedestrian at a crosswalk is a serious moving violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in a Connecticut school zone when children are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: Connecticut school zones have a 20 mph speed limit when children are present or zone warning lights are flashing. Always reduce speed well before entering the zone and remain alert for children near the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a school bus stops on a two-lane Connecticut road and displays flashing red lights?
options: a:Stop only if driving behind the bus,b:Slow to 15 mph and pass carefully,c:Stop in both directions at least 10 feet from the bus until lights stop flashing,d:Yield only if children are visibly crossing
note: Connecticut law requires vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 10 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm. You may not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Connecticut law, what happens if a driver under 21 is found driving with any alcohol in their system?
options: a:They face only a civil fine on the first offense,b:They are subject to DUI penalties under the zero tolerance law since the legal limit is 0.02% for under-21 drivers,c:No penalty unless above 0.08%,d:Only a license warning is issued for the first offense
note: Connecticut's zero tolerance law sets an illegal BAC limit of 0.02% for drivers under 21. Any BAC at or above 0.02% results in license suspension and DUI-related penalties. This effectively prohibits any alcohol use before driving for underage drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you turn right on a red light in Connecticut?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if no pedestrians are visible,d:Only between 7 AM and 9 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Connecticut after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for 'No Turn on Red' signs — they are common at many Connecticut intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane Connecticut road, a solid yellow line is on your side of the center. You are approaching a slow-moving vehicle. May you pass?
options: a:Yes, if you can complete the pass quickly,b:Yes, if the other vehicle is going more than 15 mph below the speed limit,c:No, the solid yellow line on your side prohibits passing by crossing the center,d:Yes, if you signal for at least 100 feet first
note: A solid yellow center line on your side of the road absolutely prohibits crossing to pass another vehicle. Wait for a section where a dashed yellow line is on your side before attempting to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Connecticut for normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Connecticut recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In rain, fog, or heavy traffic, increase to 4–6 seconds. The 3-second rule gives adequate time to react to a sudden stop in front of you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Connecticut, when an emergency vehicle with sirens and lights approaches from any direction, you must:
options: a:Speed up to the next intersection and pull over,b:Stop immediately in your current lane,c:Pull to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed,d:Move to the left lane and slow down
note: Connecticut law requires drivers to immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from any direction. Remain stopped until the vehicle has completely passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red light at a Connecticut intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Stop completely, yield to traffic, then proceed when safe,c:The signal is broken — treat as an uncontrolled intersection,d:Yield to cross traffic only
note: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign in Connecticut. Come to a complete stop, look in all directions, yield to existing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on most Connecticut interstates in rural areas?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Connecticut's maximum interstate speed limit is 65 mph. Urban sections and portions near Hartford and New Haven are frequently posted at lower limits. Always follow posted signs — Connecticut does not have 70 mph rural interstates like some western states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: For a newly licensed 16- or 17-year-old driver in Connecticut, who is allowed in the vehicle as a passenger during the first six months?
options: a:Only immediate family members.,b:Only a licensed driving instructor, parents/guardians, or one qualified trainer age 20+.,c:Any passenger under the age of 21.,d:Up to three non-family passengers.
note: During the first six months of holding a license, a 16- or 17-year-old Connecticut driver may only carry a licensed driving instructor, parents or a legal guardian, or one person who is at least 20 years old and has held a license for 4+ consecutive years without suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Connecticut's implied consent law, refusing to take a chemical test after a DUI stop results in:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a constitutional right,b:A 6-month license suspension for a first refusal,c:Only a fine with no license action,d:A warning on your first offense
note: Connecticut's implied consent law means that driving on public roads constitutes consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 6-month license suspension separate from any DUI charges. Refusal can also be used as evidence in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Connecticut, what does a solid white line at a crosswalk or intersection indicate?
options: a:A no-parking zone,b:A stop line — you must stop before the line at a stop sign or red light,c:A bike lane boundary,d:The edge of the travel lane
note: A solid white line across the road at an intersection is a stop line. You must stop with your front wheels behind this line when a stop sign or red light requires a stop. Rolling past the stop line and then stopping is a violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Connecticut law, who must wear a seatbelt, and what is the fine for failing to do so?
options: a:Only front-seat occupants; the fine is $50.,b:Only passengers under 18; the fine is $100.,c:All drivers and passengers must wear seatbelts; the fine is $75 for each violator.,d:Only the driver; the fine is $25.
note: Connecticut law requires all drivers and passengers to wear a seatbelt. If either the driver or any passenger fails to do so, they can be cited individually and fined $75.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following cell phone restrictions applies to 16- and 17-year-old drivers in Connecticut?
options: a:They may use hands-free cell phones only.,b:They may use cell phones at any time.,c:They may not use any cell phone or mobile electronic device, even if hands-free.,d:They may only use cell phones for text messaging.
note: In Connecticut, learner's permit holders and 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers are strictly prohibited from using any cell phone (including hands-free devices) or mobile electronic devices while driving, except in an emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver with a Connecticut learner's permit is driving alone at 7 PM on a Tuesday. Is this legal?
options: a:Yes, permit holders may drive alone during daylight hours only,b:No, permit holders must always drive with a licensed adult at least 20 years old in the front seat,c:Yes, learner's permit holders have no passenger restrictions,d:No, permit holders may only drive on weekends
note: Connecticut learner's permit holders must always be accompanied by a licensed adult at least 20 years old sitting in the front passenger seat. Driving alone on a learner's permit is illegal regardless of the time of day.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Connecticut law, when are you required to turn on your vehicle's headlights?
options: a:Only from 8:00 PM to 6:00 AM.,b:From sunset to sunrise, when visibility is less than 500 feet, and whenever you use your windshield wipers.,c:Only during heavy rain or snow storms.,d:Only when driving on highways after dark.
note: Connecticut law requires drivers to turn on headlights from sunset to sunrise, whenever visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet, and any time windshield wipers are in use due to rain, snow, or sleet.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making it dangerous to drive after drinking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or to warn of immediate danger. Do not use it to show anger, impatience, or to punish other drivers for mistakes.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked, when pedestrians are in or approaching your lane. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter driving is more dangerous because there are more hours of darkness and road surfaces can become slippery or obscured by ice, snow, and fog. These conditions reduce traction and visibility, requiring slower speeds and greater following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. Safe drivers always stay ready to yield, even when they legally have the right-of-way, if yielding will prevent a collision.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down. Once it is under control and speed has dropped, steer gradually off the road and brake gently if needed. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Alcohol begins to affect judgment and reaction time with the first drink. Even one drink can impair your ability to drive safely, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to metabolize it and lower your BAC. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roads are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of cars, including stopping at red lights and stop signs and riding in the same direction as traffic.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must wear both. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder, not the neck or under the arm. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility makes it hard to judge oncoming traffic and can lead to serious head‑on collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as another vehicle on your right. Who has the right of way?
options: a:You have the right of way because you are on the left,b:The vehicle on your right has the right of way,c:Whoever is going straight has priority,d:The larger vehicle has priority
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a 4-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right of way. The yield-to-the-right rule is a universal standard in the United States. Always be cautious — another driver may not follow the rule correctly.

question: Driving noticeably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad, but you must not drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or endanger other traffic.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may not expect it and may make sudden or risky lane changes or passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and adjust your speed reasonably for conditions, such as bad weather, without becoming an unnecessary obstruction.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task—your eyes from the road, your mind from driving, or your hands from the wheel. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of traffic.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle at night so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and eyes. High beams can blind or distract the driver ahead, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: How must you treat a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.
note: A pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is considered blind or visually impaired and must always be given the right-of-way. Slow down or stop well in advance, never crowd them or honk, and allow them to cross at their own pace anywhere they are legally crossing, not just at corners.

question: A driver should keep watch over which areas around the vehicle?
options: a:Only directly in front.,b:Beside, ahead, and to the rear of the vehicle.,c:Only the rearview mirror.,d:Only in the direction of travel.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan all around their vehicle—far ahead, to both sides, and behind using mirrors. This helps you spot hazards early, adjust speed or lane position, and avoid sudden emergencies.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction on water (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,c:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
note: When hydroplaning, your tires are riding on water instead of the road. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually without sudden braking or steering. Hard braking can cause a skid and complete loss of control.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road regardless.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park.,c:Leave the vehicle in neutral to relieve brake pressure.,d:Always point the wheels toward the center of the road.
note: On any hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park (or in gear with a manual). Turn the front wheels so if the vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb or away from traffic, not down the hill into the roadway.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle in the roadway, what is the safest action?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,c:Shift into neutral while driving through it.,d:Speed up to create a wake and drive through.
note: Deep water can cause hydroplaning, engine damage, or loss of control. If you can safely avoid a deep puddle, do so. If you must drive through water, slow down, keep a steady speed, and stay in the shallowest part.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: When animals are near the road, slow down and be prepared to stop. Animals can move unpredictably into your path. Do not speed up or swerve suddenly, as that can cause you to lose control or hit another vehicle.

question: Which action can reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Always signal when changing lanes.,c:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,d:Tailgate slower drivers to encourage them.
note: Always signal before changing lanes so other drivers know what you intend to do. Clear communication helps prevent surprises, misunderstandings, and aggressive reactions that can lead to road rage.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.,d:Treat it as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,c:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, turn on your hazard lights and carefully steer off the roadway to a safe place. Making your vehicle visible and getting out of moving traffic reduces the risk of a collision.

question: If bad weather reduces your visibility, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: When visibility is reduced by bad weather, slow down and increase your following distance. The extra space gives you more time to see hazards and stop safely if traffic ahead slows or stops.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and is blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.,b:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look straight ahead in your lane.
note: At night, if oncoming high beams are blinding you, do not look directly at the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to keep your vehicle centered until the other car passes.

question: Regulatory road signs are commonly what color background?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:White.,d:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations you must obey, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. In the U.S., these are most commonly white rectangles with black, red, or green symbols or lettering, which is why white is the standard background color associated with regulatory signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when should you reduce your speed?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: On an interstate, you should maintain highway speed until you are actually in the deceleration lane. Once you enter the deceleration lane, then begin slowing to the advisory or posted speed for the exit ramp. Slowing too early on the main roadway can surprise faster traffic behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you scan?
options: a:Left–right–left.,b:Left only.,c:Right–left–right.
note: Before entering an intersection, you should scan left, then right, then left again. Traffic coming from your left is closer to you and will reach the intersection sooner, so you check that direction first, then check for hazards from the right, and finally recheck the left to be sure it is still clear before you proceed.

question: No passing zone signs and markings indicate:
options: a:There are oncoming cars passing in your direction.,b:Passing is only permitted during daylight hours.,c:You cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.
note: No passing zone signs and pavement markings warn that it is unsafe to move into the oncoming lane to pass. This is usually because your view of oncoming traffic is limited by hills, curves, or other conditions, so you cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely. When you see these signs or solid yellow lines on your side, you must not pass.

question: For persons age 21 or older, what BAC level is illegal for driving?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, it is illegal for drivers age 21 or older to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. At or above this level, you are considered legally impaired, and you can be arrested and convicted of DUI even if you feel you can still drive.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,c:Brake hard and steer sharply to the right.,d:Immediately turn off the engine and coast.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay calm, and avoid sudden braking. Gently ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows down gradually, keep the vehicle going straight, and signal and steer to the shoulder or a safe place out of traffic. Once you are out of the traffic lane and under control, brake more firmly to come to a complete stop.

question: What should you do to reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, the main way to reduce the chance of losing traction or hydroplaning is to slow down. Lower speed allows your tires to maintain better contact with the road surface. You should also avoid sudden steering, hard braking, or rapid acceleration, because abrupt actions can cause skids when the road is slippery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to use extra caution but does not require a full stop. You should slow down, scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, and hazards, and proceed only when it is safe. Stop only if needed for safety or to yield the right-of-way.

question: How should you proceed when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,d:Maintain your current speed.
note: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must slow down and proceed with caution. Look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, and any vehicles that may not yield properly. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety, but you should be prepared to react quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are continually being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On expressways and other multi-lane roads, you should generally travel in the right-hand lane unless you are passing or preparing for a left turn. If vehicles are passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. Move safely to the lane on your right so faster traffic can pass on the left.

question: When you are following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Allow a larger following distance.,c:Be ready to use your horn.,d:Maintain your usual close following distance.
note: Allowing a larger following distance behind a motorcycle is important because motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles and are less stable on wet or uneven surfaces. A three- to four-second following distance gives you enough time to react if the rider slows, stops, or falls.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, how should you proceed?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.,d:Ignore them unless they step into the road.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you must slow down and pass with caution, watching carefully in case they step into the road. Be prepared to stop and always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks or when they are crossing legally.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and remove alcohol's effects from your body?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Time.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and eliminate its impairing effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, whom must you yield to?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic.,d:Only yield to vehicles, not pedestrians.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may not cross these lines to pass another vehicle; you may only cross when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the illuminated area of your headlights.,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead.,c:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be seen.,d:Drive at the posted daytime speed limit only.
note: At night you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called "overdriving your headlights" if you go too fast, because you would not be able to stop in time for hazards that appear in the lit area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed in a no passing zone, what should you do to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter the lane safely?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: If another driver is passing you, even in a no‑passing zone, you should help avoid a collision. Slightly reduce your speed so the passing driver has more space and time to return to the lane safely. Never speed up or swerve while you are being passed.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, you should:
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or road edge and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb or edge and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: a:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,b:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: Work zones often have lane shifts, workers close to traffic, and sudden slowdowns. You should avoid tailgating and leave extra following distance so you have more time to react to stopped or slowing vehicles and any unexpected changes.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, the safest first action is to ease off the accelerator. This begins to increase your following distance smoothly. Then, if needed, brake gently. Sudden hard braking or swerving can cause you to lose control or be hit from behind.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe. You must still judge distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and never cross the line if your view is blocked or you cannot complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:When the passed driver flashes their lights.
note: After passing another vehicle, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (often its headlights) in your inside rearview mirror. This helps ensure you have enough space and do not cut the other driver off. Always signal before returning to the lane.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver makes a mistake.,b:When it may help prevent a collision.,c:To encourage slow drivers to move faster.,d:To greet friends on the sidewalk.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or to warn others of a hazard when necessary. It should not be used to show anger, hurry other drivers, or greet people. Unnecessary horn use can startle others and create unsafe situations.

question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you avoid using?
options: a:Cruise control.,b:Lower gears downhill.,c:Gradual steering inputs.,d:Increased following distance.
note: On snow or ice, you should avoid using cruise control because it can cause your wheels to spin or lose traction without you noticing quickly. Instead, keep full control of your speed with the pedals, make all steering and braking inputs gradual, and increase your following distance to allow more time to react.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. Avoid driving beside them for long periods so the driver can see you and you have room to react if the truck needs to change lanes or avoid a hazard.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children riding bicycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,b:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children on bicycles are smaller, harder to see, and often less predictable than adults. They may have slower reflexes and less traffic experience, so you must give them extra space and be prepared for sudden moves.

question: Is it legal to drive while using medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:Yes, if it is prescribed by a physician.,b:Only if you do not feel drowsy.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:Only on short trips.
note: Driving is illegal if any medication or drug—prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal—impairs your ability to drive safely. The key issue is impairment, not whether a doctor prescribed it or how far you are driving.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, you should not:
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened, press your back firmly against the seat, and press your head against the head restraint. This helps reduce whiplash and other injuries.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change as speed increases?
options: a:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,b:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,c:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs a longer distance to stop, and the force of a collision increases sharply. Higher speeds mean more severe crashes and a greater chance of serious injury or death.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign indicate to drivers?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To speed up slightly.
note: A No Passing Zone sign tells you that it is unsafe and illegal to pass other vehicles in that area, usually because of limited visibility, hills, curves, or other hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you NOT do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and return from there.,b:Back up on the road or shoulder.,c:Find an alternate route beyond the exit.,d:Proceed to the next crossroad to turn around.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, never stop or back up on the freeway or shoulder. This is extremely dangerous because traffic is moving at high speed and drivers do not expect a vehicle moving in reverse. Instead, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a legal way to return to your route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing, what should you confirm?
options: a:That the passed vehicle signaled for you to return.,b:That you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:That you are one vehicle length ahead.,d:That the passed vehicle slowed down.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you are sure you have enough space. A good rule is to wait until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror. This indicates you are far enough ahead to return without cutting the other driver off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection at the posted speed when the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Proceed through the intersection without caution.,b:Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.,c:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.,d:Proceed with caution if you cannot stop safely.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking hard and risking a rear‑end collision.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect several critical driving skills at the same time. They reduce alertness, slow your reaction time, and harm coordination and judgment. Because both alertness and coordination are impaired, any amount of impairment can make it harder to notice hazards and control your vehicle safely.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than during the day?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights provide much less visibility than daylight, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce what you can see. With less time to spot hazards, you must slow down and use extra caution at night.

question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?
options: a:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,b:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, including cold medications, can make you drowsy or otherwise impair your driving. Even when taken as directed, some drugs slow your reaction time, affect judgment, or cause dizziness. You must read labels and warnings and talk with your doctor or pharmacist to understand how a medication may affect your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: When you pass another vehicle, you should move into the passing lane, accelerate to complete the pass promptly, and avoid lingering in the blind spot. Passing should always be done within the speed limit and only when you have enough clear space to return safely to your lane without cutting off the other driver.

question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed?
options: a:Driving down long, gradual hills.,b:Driving up long or steep hills.,c:Driving on level roads.,d:While passing smaller vehicles.
note: Large trucks are heavy and require a lot of power to climb. On long or steep upgrades, they often lose speed because the engine is working harder against gravity. Expect trucks to slow down on hills and adjust your driving so you do not follow too closely or cut in front of them.

question: Which of the following substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough or cold medicines that contain codeine or antihistamines. These drugs can cause drowsiness, slow reactions, and affect judgment. Always check medication labels and warnings and avoid driving if a drug may make you less alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning left on red is legal only when:
options: a:You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,b:You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.,c:You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: In most U.S. states, you may turn left on a red light only after stopping completely and only when turning from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, unless a sign prohibits it. You must yield to pedestrians and all other traffic that has the right‑of‑way before making the turn.

question: What behavior describes defensive driving?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, behind, and to the sides, checking mirrors often, and watching for potential hazards so you can react early and safely.

question: When stopping on snow or ice while driving a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent skidding and maintain steering control on snow or ice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Looking over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Checking for drivers entering the same lane.,c:Moving into another lane while inside an intersection.,d:Signaling before changing lanes.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in an intersection because traffic is crossing and conditions can change quickly. Instead, stay in your lane through the intersection, then change lanes when you are clear and it is safe.

question: How close may you park to a fire hydrant?
options: a:Within 15 feet.,b:Within 10 feet.,c:Within 20 feet.,d:Within 5 feet.
note: In most U.S. states, you must not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant so firefighters have enough room to connect hoses and work quickly in an emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a left turn when turning from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, you should start from the lane closest to the left curb and turn into the first legal lane on the road you are entering, unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you must:
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap and any required signal (green light or green arrow) allows the turn, then complete the turn without cutting off oncoming traffic or pedestrians.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,b:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:Alcohol affects judgement, which is needed to drive safely.
note: Alcohol slows your reactions and affects judgment, coordination, and vision even at low levels. You can be unsafe to drive even if you feel fine or are under the legal limit, so you should never rely on how you feel or simple tests like walking a straight line to decide if you can drive.

question: To be aware of traffic behind you, you should:
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Safe drivers regularly check their rearview and side mirrors so they know what is happening behind and to the sides of their vehicle. This helps you adjust speed, change lanes safely, and react early if another driver is approaching too fast or following too closely.

question: What must you do when you approach an eight-sided (octagonal) sign?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Stop completely at the sign.,c:Turn if the way is clear.,d:Yield and proceed without stopping.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign is always a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic with the right-of-way and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a red light is showing but a green arrow is also displayed, when may you proceed in the arrow direction?
options: a:First come to a complete stop.,b:Wait until the light changes.,c:Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if the main light is red. You may proceed only if you are in the correct lane for that arrow and the intersection is clear, yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign indicates:
options: a:Yield.,b:Stop.,c:Warning.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, merging traffic, or construction zones. They are typically yellow for general warnings and orange in work zones.

question: You should always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks. Only proceed when there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. Trains can come at any time and cannot stop quickly, so you must be sure you can fully cross before entering the crossing.

question: What is a likely effect of tailgating another vehicle?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Reduces collisions by preventing being 'cut off.',c:Cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Tailgating, or following too closely, increases the risk of rear-end collisions and can anger or intimidate other drivers. It is unsafe, can lead to road rage, and may result in a citation for following too closely or careless driving.

question: From top to bottom, what is the proper order of traffic lights?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Red, yellow, green,d:Yellow
note: On a standard vertical traffic signal, the lights are arranged red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom. This order helps drivers quickly recognize the signal even from a distance or in poor visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permitted to pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken (dashed) line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe and legal to do so. A solid line next to your lane means no passing. You must also avoid passing on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots can be eliminated with one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked using your rearview mirror alone.,d:Mirrors always show everything around your car.
note: Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind, directly in front, and along both sides. Even with properly adjusted mirrors, every vehicle still has blind spots, so you must turn your head to check them before changing lanes or merging.

question: Approaching a steady yellow light at an intersection, what should you do if you have not entered the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce speed and prepare to stop; stop if you can do so safely.,c:Come to a safe stop no matter what.,d:Increase your speed and proceed.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and be prepared to stop, and you must stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. Do not speed up to beat the red light.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in fog.,b:Constantly staring at the road ahead.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,d:Driving with only parking lights on.
note: Safe drivers scan all around them, including checking rearview and side mirrors frequently to know what is happening behind and beside their vehicle. Staring straight ahead causes you to miss hazards, and high beams in fog create glare that makes it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not for driving.

question: To check a blind spot before changing lanes, where should you look?
options: a:Only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Over your left or right shoulder to view the blind spot.,c:Only the left outside mirror.,d:Only the left-side window.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors first, then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. This head check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles hidden beside you.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When they are wet after several hours of rain.,c:When they are clean and dry.,d:During freezing temperatures only.
note: Roads are usually most slippery just after it starts to rain because oil and other residues on the pavement mix with the first water and rise to the surface. After it has rained for a while, much of this washes away and traction generally improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow centerlines on roads?
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate lanes moving in the same direction.,d:Mark bicycle lanes.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and also indicate that passing is allowed when it can be done safely and is not otherwise prohibited by signs or additional markings.

question: By how much should you reduce your speed when driving on packed snow?
options: a:One-third.,b:One-quarter.,c:One-half.
note: On packed snow, you should reduce your normal speed by about half. Snow greatly reduces traction, so driving at roughly 50% of your usual dry‑road speed helps you maintain control and gives you more distance to stop safely.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve visibility without as much glare.

question: Combining a prescription drug with alcohol can:
options: a:Make you more alert.,b:There will likely be no effect.,c:Make you unfit to drive.
note: Combining alcohol with many prescription or over‑the‑counter drugs can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment. This makes you unsafe and legally unfit to drive, even if each substance alone might seem mild.

question: You should always travel at:
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At the speed limit.
note: You must choose a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions while never exceeding the posted speed limit. In poor conditions, the safe speed is often lower than the limit, even if other drivers are going faster.

question: Which of the following statements about seat belt use is false?
options: a:They prevent a 'human collision' by holding you in place.,b:They are not necessary if your vehicle has an airbag.,c:They keep you from being thrown from the vehicle in the event of an accident.
note: Seat belts are essential safety equipment in every vehicle, even if it has airbags. Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Seat belts keep you in position so the airbag can protect you correctly, prevent you from hitting the interior of the car, and greatly reduce the chance of being ejected in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following persons' instructions must drivers obey?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Drivers must always obey instructions from authorized traffic control personnel, including flaggers at construction or maintenance sites. Flaggers help direct traffic safely around work zones and protect both workers and drivers. Instructions from other drivers or private security in parking lots are not legally binding in the same way as those from authorized traffic control officials.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your visibility, you should drive more slowly and turn on your:
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: When dust, smoke, or similar conditions reduce visibility, you should slow down and turn on your low-beam headlights. This helps you see the road and makes your vehicle more visible to others. Emergency flashers are for stopped or very slow-moving vehicles in specific situations, and parking lights alone are not sufficient for driving in low-visibility conditions.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:You must always drive carefully at railroad crossings and never proceed if a train is approaching.,b:You should never stop your vehicle on the railroad tracks.,c:You must stop when directed to do so by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,d:All of the above.
note: At railroad crossings, you must stop when directed by a flagger, a stop sign, or active warning devices such as flashing red lights or gates. Even when not required to stop, you must slow down, look, and listen for trains, and never proceed if a train is approaching or if you cannot safely clear the tracks.

question: Which is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.,d:Driving below the posted work zone speed.
note: In work zones, following too closely and failing to watch for workers, equipment, and changing traffic patterns are both dangerous behaviors. Work zones often have sudden stops, lane shifts, and workers close to moving traffic, so you must leave extra space, reduce speed as posted, and stay highly alert. Simply driving below the posted work zone speed is not inherently dangerous if done safely and appropriately for conditions.

question: What happens as your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More sober.,c:More coordinated.
note: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, alcohol has a stronger effect on your brain and body. Your judgment, coordination, and reaction time become more impaired, which means you are more intoxicated and less able to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit should be driven only under which conditions?
options: a:During the day.,b:During the night.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you may legally drive only when conditions are ideal—good weather, good visibility, light traffic, and a safe road surface. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions, you must drive slower than the posted maximum.

question: If you drive too fast on a wet road, what danger may occur?
options: a:Your tires will start to glide over the water.,b:Your ability to judge speed and control will be impaired.,c:Your own spray will obscure the vision of other drivers.
note: On a wet road at higher speeds, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride up on a thin layer of water, a condition called hydroplaning. When this happens, you can lose steering and braking control, greatly increasing the risk of a crash.

question: What should you do when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.,b:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Gravel and dirt roads provide less traction than paved roads because the surface is loose. Your tires can slip more easily, so you must slow down, allow more distance to stop, and avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration.

question: If you reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Slow down and drive around the gates.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.,c:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop and remain stopped well behind the gates. Do not drive around or under the gates. Proceed only after the train has passed, the lights stop flashing, and the gates are fully raised, and you have checked that the tracks are clear.

question: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended after driving with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:0.08 percent or more.,b:Any amount.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: For drivers under 21, many states, including Connecticut, use a zero-tolerance standard. Any measurable amount of alcohol in the blood can result in license suspension because drivers under the legal drinking age are not allowed to drive with alcohol in their system.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:Through vibration and sound, they alert inattentive drivers that their vehicles have left the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that create noise and vibration when you drive over them. This alerts inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, giving them time to correct their path.

question: What is the safest response if you encounter an aggressive driver?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, your priority is safety, not winning or teaching them a lesson. Create space, avoid eye contact or gestures, and let them pass or move away from you. This reduces the chance of a confrontation or collision.

question: Which area is most likely to be icy after snow or rain on cold days?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Shaded areas of the road freeze first and thaw last because they receive less sunlight. After snow or rain on cold days, ice can remain in shaded spots even when the rest of the road looks clear, so you should slow down and be especially cautious there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You enter a left-turn lane for an upcoming turn and see oncoming traffic. What should you do first?
options: a:Move to the left of the center lane.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.
note: Before making a left turn, you should signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before the turn—so other drivers know your intentions. Stay in the proper turn lane with your wheels pointed straight until you actually begin the turn; if your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do at an intersection?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:Continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you are allowed to proceed straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection or lawfully within it. Green never means to speed up; it means you may go with caution.

question: How can sudden highway wind gusts affect vehicles?
options: a:They generally affect only large vehicles.,b:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,c:They only reduce visibility.,d:They have no effect on vehicles.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, making it harder to stay in your lane and control steering. While large vehicles and vehicles with high profiles are especially affected, all vehicles can be destabilized. Wind can also blow dust, sand, or debris, which may reduce visibility and create additional hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. The side with the broken line is allowed to cross the center line to pass when it is safe and legal. The side with the solid line must not cross to pass. This helps control where passing is allowed on two-way roads.

question: How should you approach the right-of-way rules when driving?
options: a:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: Right-of-way rules say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. You should always be ready to yield, even if you are legally entitled to go, if yielding will help avoid a collision. Defensive drivers never insist on their right-of-way when it would create a dangerous situation.

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Keep your wheels facing straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road and set the parking brake. If the vehicle starts to roll, the front tire will move toward the shoulder or off the roadway instead of into traffic. With a curb, you turn the wheels away from the curb when parking uphill.

question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway in bad weather, how should you follow?
options: a:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,c:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.
note: Large trucks block your view of the road ahead and need more distance to stop. In bad weather, increase your following distance even more so you have time to react and can see around the truck. Never follow closely or tailgate a large vehicle.

question: Which action helps prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. Slowing down in wet conditions helps your tires maintain traction and reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warning signs.,b:General warning signs.,c:Red.
note: Orange traffic signs are used in construction and maintenance areas. They warn you of road work, lane shifts, workers, and equipment ahead, so you should slow down and be prepared for changing conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and where you have a clear view ahead. You must never pass in an intersection or on a curve or hill where your view of oncoming traffic is blocked.

question: What message appears on a red octagonal sign?
options: a:One-way.,b:Do not enter.,c:Stop.
note: A red octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles to your right and left arrive simultaneously, yield to:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle when:
options: a:Where there is a red traffic light.,b:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must stop at a steady or flashing red light and whenever a police officer directing traffic orders you to stop. Traffic signals and lawful orders from officers both override your right-of-way.

question: If you must park in an area not normally used for parking, you should:
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: If you must park where vehicles are not usually parked, position your vehicle so it can be clearly seen by drivers from all directions. Good visibility reduces the chance of a collision with passing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered it, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce you speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to get through.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly to slow down.,c:Pull over immediately onto the roadway without slowing.,d:Speed up to reach the shoulder.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the gas, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Brake gently only after you have the car under control, then steer to a safe place off the road. Sudden or hard braking can cause you to lose control.

question: From which areas of your vehicle must you remove snow, ice, and frost before driving?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows and mirrors.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Before driving, clear snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors so you have an unobstructed view in every direction. Snow or ice left on glass or mirrors can block your vision and create dangerous blind spots.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and may not go in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or a green arrow appears. It works like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
